dedupe_keys.name: idea integrated dashboard for energy transition analysis

description: IDEA (Integrated Dashboard for Energy Transition Analysis) is an open-source visualisation dashboard for energy model inputs and outputs, developed by the SESIT group at the University of Victoria. The G-PST Open Tools Portal says modellers use it during model development to check inputs and outputs and analysts use it to explore results. It runs on its own from its GitLab repository or inside the M3 modelling platform, where it launches after a model run. Coverage: the portal lists dashboards for COPPER (emissions, capacity, new capacity, supply, transmission flow, dispatch) and SILVER (optimal power flow costs and results, prices, unit commitment results), with more models planned. Format and access: Python source on GitLab (sesit/idea); the README explains how to add a model profile with its own folder structure. The repository's last activity was 2 September 2024. Licence: MIT (portal). Caveats: installation steps and supported data formats beyond the model profiles were not read; activity has been quiet since 2024. Simulation uses: inspecting and presenting capacity expansion and dispatch results from energy system models. Related records: COPPER (model-copper-canadian-electricity-capacity-expansion) and SILVER (model-silver-variable-renewable-electricity-dispatch) are the models it visualises.
